currentContext.business: The Company is predominantly engaged in the manufacture and/or sale of a wide range of Power Cables from 1.1 kV to 400 kV, Wires and Conductors, Accessories for Cables and Conductors, products for quality power solutions viz. Capacitors and Capacitor Banks, Harmonic Filters, etc. and Turnkey Projects relating thereto. It is also a manufacturer of Power and Control Cables, Optical Fibre Cables and Capacitors, and is actively engaged in executing turnkey projects in the Transmission and Distribution (T&D) segment of the power sector. Its EHV cable facility uses India's first of its kind VCV (Vertical Continuous Vulcanization) technology and is also equipped to manufacture EHV HVDC cables, serving power utilities (State and Central) and private-sector customers in India and 32 overseas countries.

Quality Power Solutions: MV automatic power factor control panels

currentContext.expansion: Universal Cables' entire growth plan is based on organic expansion, and the Company states it sees enough growth opportunities within its existing facilities to implement expansion plans for scaling up manufacturing capacity of LV, MV, HV & EHV Power Cables, flexible wire and multicore Flexible Cables, Capacitors, etc. During FY 2025-26 two projects were completed: the capacity expansion of the flexible wire and Multicore Flexible Cables facility at Verna (Goa), operational at the end of October 2025, and a new Low Voltage power cable facility at Satna (M.P.), operational at the end of March 2026. The larger MV and EHV cables capacity augmentation project was partially commissioned for commercial operations during the third quarter of the year under review and is likely to be fully operational in phased manner by end of August/September 2026; the Company has flagged minor delays in fully operationalising it due to civil construction related delays and other external factors, and says the enhanced capacity will significantly strengthen its MV and EHV manufacturing capabilities. Alongside this, the Company has planned technological upgradation and modernisation of its EHV cable facility at Satna with an outlay of Rs 7300 Lakhs, investing in precision manufacturing and flexibility to meet use-case-specific quality standards and international quality, safety and environmental standards, with the aim of becoming more competitive and export oriented. Beyond cables, the Company is investing in setting up infrastructure for manufacturing and sale of HTLS (High Temperature Low Sag) Conductors with TS Aluminium Encapsulated Composite Core, and plans in-house production of HVDC cables, which are currently imported, ahead of multiple government HVDC projects. Capital expenditure during the year was directed primarily towards production capacity augmentation initiatives aimed at supporting future growth. On the sustainability side, the Company operates rooftop solar plants of 2 MW at Satna and 0.5 MW at Goa plus electricity from a 4 MW wind-solar hybrid project commissioned in July 2024 under a long-term Power Purchase Agreement, and is installing two new sewage treatment plants of 32 KLD and 16 KLD capacity expected to be commissioned in FY 2026-27 on top of existing STP capacity of 200 + 70 KLD.
currentContext.mdna: Government schemes - RDSS, Green Energy Corridor, PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana, National Smart Grid Mission and FAME II - are collectively driving additions to line length, sub-station capacity, smart metering and EV charging infrastructure, shaping a broad and durable demand base.|Discoms and city utilities are shifting from overhead lines to underground cabling, with metro rail networks, smart city clusters, commercial districts and dense residential zones mandating 11kV and 33kV underground systems, ring main units and compact substations - accelerating uptake of medium-voltage and high-performance cables.|India's wires and cables industry constitutes about 40% of the electrical industry and is expected to grow 2x GDP growth during FY 2025-2030, driven by capacity expansion, the T&D and real-estate capex cycle and emerging segments such as data centres, EV and mobility, railways and metro expansion.|Per the Crisil Intelligence Report of February 2026, domestic power cable consumption may grow about 22% in FY 2025-26 after about 45% growth in FY 2024-25, and is expected to grow at a CAGR of 9-11% between FY 2026-27 and FY 2028-29.|Management expects revenue growth higher than the industry, driven by increased focus on exports, successful completion of prestigious export orders for EHV cables up to 400 kV, and orders in hand as well as in the pipeline.|EHV Power Cables: VCV lines dedicated to EHV production are fully aligned to meet the anticipated surge in EHV demand, giving a competitive edge through superior product quality and faster delivery timelines; risks.risk: Raw Material Price Risk - copper, aluminium, lead and polymer volatility against largely firm-price cable contracts
risks.note: The prices of international commodities such as copper, aluminium, lead and polymers, the key raw material components, are subject to considerable price volatility, while market prices of cables are generally on a firm price basis. Strict implementation of Quality Control Order(s) by the Government without adequate and competitive local production facilities matching global quality standards for key inputs adds further price-volatility risk and unjustified price increases, and 'green inflation' risk remains high because aluminium and copper have higher-application use cases in energy transition products.

risks.risk: Working Capital Risk - dependence on infrastructure/industrial capex, budgetary allocations and institutional funding
risks.note: The Company caters to infrastructural and industrial segments that largely depend on economic buoyancy, budgetary allocation and funding from banks and institutions. An economic setback or curtailment in fund allocation could lead to fund scarcity and delayed realisation of receivables, directly affecting working capital requirements. Mitigated by prioritising customers with sound financial standing, constant follow-up on receivables and lean, symmetric inventories.

risks.risk: Competition Risk and technology obsolescence - distinct competitive dynamics by voltage grade
risks.note: In EHV, competition comes from both Indian and overseas manufacturers, with entry barriers requiring performance-record credentials from users on supply and installation to qualify as an eligible bidder plus repeat testing and revalidation of type/design test reports; the Company must keep pace with multinational development and innovation to avoid obsolescence. In HV & MV, new entrants pose price-competitiveness risk. The LV segment is intensely competitive with a proliferation of regional producers of low-quality, low-margin products that has been pernicious to the health of the organised sector.

risks.risk: Market Demand Risk - historically cyclical power cable demand and direct exposure to Government policy
risks.note: Demand for power cables has historically been cyclical, and the Company is dependent on the infrastructure sector, industries and OEMs, with Government policies having a direct bearing on demand from various market segments. Partially offset by a broad-based clientele, wide product range and a flexible manufacturing set-up that allows product-mix changes to suit the order and demand pattern.

risks.risk: Project execution and Liquidated Damage Risk on turnkey contracts
risks.note: The Company executes several turnkey projects requiring statutory right-of-way permissions from authorities that are outside the control of both the Company and the user, which may defer projects and cause blockage of receivables and cost over-runs. Separately, intense competition forces acceptance of short delivery contracts, and failure to meet the delivery period exposes the Company to imposition of liquidated damages.

risks.risk: Customer Risk - customer priority shifts, increasing customer power and over-reliance on major customers
risks.note: The Company is prone to the risk of customers' priority shift, increasing customer power and over-reliance on major customers. Mitigated by staying in constant touch with clientele, providing technical guidance and crisis support to remain 'virtually indispensable', and building a preferred-supplier reputation that creates a quality trust barrier against competition and new entrants.

risks.risk: External trade barriers, geopolitical fragmentation and rising ESG compliance cost
risks.note: Global power cables and capacitors trade is increasingly exposed to trade policies and tariffs aimed at protecting local manufacturing, alongside growing protectionism, supply chain disruption, recalibration of international alliances and economic nationalism. Escalating raw material and logistics costs, supply chain bottlenecks from geo-political developments, regional conflicts and social unrest may impact operations. Implementing sustainable manufacturing practices under stringent environment and safety regulations is costly and complex, with limited availability of sustainable materials and standardisation challenges.

risks.risk: Occupational Health & Safety and environmental footprint of operations (BRSR material issues)
risks.note: BRSR identifies Occupational Health & Safety as a risk given injury and fatality rates higher than in many other industries, with temporary workers more vulnerable due to limited training and experience; inadequate management can lead to serious human harm, legal consequences and significant financial burdens (accidents increase insurance, litigation and downtime costs). Environmental footprint of operations is also flagged as a risk - biodiversity impact, air emissions, water discharge, natural resource depletion and waste generation - with non-compliance penalties as the stated financial implication.
